item.text: {"analysis":"The attention-augmented ConvRec achieved host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5038, improving on the reported convolution-only result of 0.4962 but remaining slightly below SASRec’s 0.505. Category HR@10 was 0.520 Movies_and_TV, 0.580 Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.380 Electronics, and 0.535 CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics remained the weakest category. The aggregate gain supports further investigation of content-dependent historical selection, but does not establish that attention caused the improvement or recovered both prior category regressions; prior category scores were not supplied. The trial succeeded operationally and consumed 479.51 allocated GPU-seconds.","code_summary":"One independent network and one selected checkpoint per category. ConvRec uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, jointly learned item biases, and eight causal convolutional residual blocks with dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8]. One pre-normalized, two-head causal self-attention residual follows the convolution stack, with attention and residual dropout 0.2, then final LayerNorm; no additional feed-forward block. Combined causal/padding masks permit a diagonal entry for fully masked queries and explicitly zero padded outputs. Training retains random-prefix sampling, 32-negative cross-entropy, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, gradient clipping, and validation HR@10 checkpoint selection with NDCG@10 tie-breaking and 25-epoch patience. Runtime checks cover finite outputs/gradients, causality, and serialization parity. The generated predictor imports the revised architecture and strictly loads one checkpoint for each of the four dataset routes; no averaging or separately fitted scoring components."}
